rounds.text: The business is demonstrating exceptional top-line and bottom-line acceleration, with compounded sales growth reaching 79% over the trailing twelve months [E15] and net profit surging 103% year-on-year [E61]. Operating margins have expanded by 7 percentage points over three years to 10% in the TTM period [E22], while Q1 FY27 EBITDA grew 111% year-on-year to reach an EBITDA margin of 15.48% [E77]. This financial performance is supported by strong operational momentum, including 100% capacity utilization at the Palwal facility [E81] and upcoming expansions such as the 6,000 metric ton per annum LFP battery recycling plant in Sampla, which is set to become operational in the next two to three months [E75, E86]. Furthermore, profits are fully backed by cash with a cash conversion ratio of 1.12x for March 2026 [E26], and institutional confidence is rising as evidenced by foreign institutions increasing their holding to 1.29% alongside positive institutional money flow [E34, E36]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 55.8x and a price-to-book ratio of 8.00x [E1, E2], while a discounted cash flow model indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 55 per share against a market price of Rs 172 [E37].

Nupur Recyclers Ltd trades at an excessive P/E of 55.8x [E1] and a P/B of 8.00x [E2], which towers over the sector benchmark P/E of 60.22x against 14.11x [E6] and a sector P/B of 8.9x against 1.88x [E7]. This lofty valuation leaves a staggering negative margin of safety of -213.4% [E38], as a discounted cash flow analysis pegs intrinsic value at a mere Rs 55 per share compared to a market price of Rs 172 [E37]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands an aggressive 20.7% earnings growth, vastly outstripping the base case assumption of 5.0% [E39]. Operating margins have shown an inconsistent yearly trend over the last two years [E24], and the company offers a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], choosing to withhold payouts to conserve profits [E83]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing twelve months sales and profit growth of 79% [E15] and 69% [E17], alongside positive institutional money flow [E36].

Conceded: the stock trades at elevated valuation multiples, including a P/E of 55.8x and a P/B of 8.00x [E1, E2], alongside a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 55 per share against a market price of Rs 172 [E37]. However, dismissing the company on valuation alone ignores massive fundamental acceleration, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 79% [E15] and a profit growth of 69% [E17], which easily outstrips typical cyclical baselines. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], but retained earnings are directly funding critical high-return expansions, such as the new Sampla facility for LFP battery recycling and aluminium ingots designed to capture secular EV demand [E74, E75, E82]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded significantly to 10% in TTM from 3% three years prior [E22], demonstrating improving operational leverage rather than stagnant pricing power. Finally, the bear's fear of stretched expectations is countered by positive institutional money flow [E36] and robust profitability metrics, with ROCE reaching 14.2% against a sector benchmark of 11.68% [E10].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth reached 79% and profit growth hit 69% [E15, E17]. However, the bull's reliance on these growth figures ignores the fact that compounded sales and profit growth over a three-year period both crawl at a meager 5% [E14, E16], revealing that recent acceleration is a sharp short-term anomaly rather than a steady compounding track record. While the bull points to retained earnings funding expansions like the Sampla facility [E74, E75, E82], the market price of ₹172 [E2] demands a staggering 20.7% perpetual earnings growth under a reverse DCF, far outstripping the base-case expectation of 5.0% [E39]. Conceded: operating margins expanded to 10% in the TTM period [E22]. Yet, the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are officially flagged as inconsistent [E24, E25], and reported earnings carry a vulnerability note regarding ₹14.0 Cr of other income [E56] alongside creeping debtor days from 30.9 to 38.4 [E57]. Finally, citing ROCE of 14.2% [E10] does not excuse paying an astronomical P/E of 55.8x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 35.12x against sector benchmarks of 9.17x [E11], leaving investors exposed to a severe -213.4% margin of safety and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown risk of -66.3% [E38, E45].

Conceded: the 3-year compounded sales and profit growth sit at 5% [E14, E16], and the reverse DCF indicates a 20.7% growth expectation [E39]. However, dismissing the recent acceleration as an anomaly ignores the TTM sales growth of 79% and profit growth of 69% [E15, E17], alongside Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue jumping to approximately ₹83.03 crore and EBITDA climbing 111% year-on-year [E76, E77]. Conceded: the operating-margin trend is flagged as inconsistent [E24, E25]. Yet, management explicitly guides that margins will not fall back to earlier levels of 10% to 12% and could range from 10% to 25% [E70], supported by Q1 FY27 EBITDA margins expanding to 15.48% [E77]. While the bear highlights debtor days increasing to 38.4 [E57], the company maintains a robust cash conversion of 1.12x with operating cash flow fully backing reported profits at ₹18 Cr [E26, E27]. Furthermore, pointing to valuation multiples overlooks the structural catalysts already nearing completion, including the Sampla LFP battery recycling facility and the expanded Nupur Extrusion capacity scaling up by this financial year end [E75, E87].

Conceded: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew to approximately ₹83.03 crore and EBITDA jumped 111% year-on-year [E76, E77]. However, the bull's reliance on this short-term acceleration ignores the stagnant 3-year compounded sales and profit growth of just 5% [E14, E16]. While the bull points to management guidance and Q1 EBITDA margins reaching 15.48% [E70, E77], the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E24, E25]. Conceded: operating cash flow fully backs reported profits at 1.12x [E26], but debtor days have simultaneously increased from 30.9 to 38.4 days [E57]. Furthermore, pointing to upcoming structural projects like the Sampla facility does not excuse a rich valuation of 55.8x P/E and 8.00x price-to-book [E1, E2] where today's price already demands a steep 20.7% earnings growth rate [E39].

Management expects margins to fluctuate within a range and could be around 10% to 25%, without falling back to earlier levels of 10% to 12%.
evidence.quote: Going forward, margins may fluctuate within a range and could be around 10%–25%. However, we do not expect the margins to fall back to the earlier levels of around 10%–12%.

evidence.fact: Nupur Extrusion operates its Haryana facility catering to solar plant manufacturing and OEM customers, which are seeing strong, secular demand.
evidence.quote: Nupur Extrusion Private Limited operates our Haryana facility and is currently running at 1800 MT per annum capacity against total production capacity of 2400 MT per annum, catering to solar plant manufacturing and OEM (original equipment manufacturer) customers, both segments seeing strong, secular demand in India today.

evidence.fact: Management noted that India's lithium-ion battery recycling industry is expected to grow rapidly as electric vehicle adoption scales up.
evidence.quote: India's lithium-ion battery recycling industry is still at an early stage, but expected to grow rapidly as electric vehicle adoption scale up.

evidence.fact: Frank Metals plans further capacity expansion in the aluminium extrusion business over the medium term.
evidence.quote: Frank Metals plans further capacity expansion here, with the objective of building a scalable aluminium extrusion business over the medium term.

evidence.fact: A new facility in Sampla, Haryana is under construction to produce 200 metric tons per month of zinc and aluminium ingots.
evidence.quote: Our new facility in Sampla, it's coming and it's under construction phase. We will produce zinc ingot, aluminum ingots in it with 200 metric ton per month under construction.

evidence.fact: A new world-class facility for LFP battery recycling with a capacity of 6,000 metric tons per annum is in the construction phase at Sampla.
evidence.quote: New facility at Sampla, NRL. Again, we are coming with a world-class facility of LFP battery and we recycle 6,000 per metric ton per annum. It's, it's in a construction phase.

evidence.fact: Consolidated total revenue for Q1 FY27 stood at approximately INR 83.03 crore compared to INR 53.03 crore in Q1 FY26.
evidence.quote: On a consolidate basis, our total revenue for Q1 FY27 stood at approximately INR83.03 crore compared to INR53.03 crore in Q1 FY26.

evidence.fact: EBITDA for Q1 FY27 came in at approximately INR 12.86 crore, translating into an EBITDA margin of 15.48%.
evidence.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter came in at approximately INR12.86 crore compared to INR6.08 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR6.83 crore in Q4 FY26, a growth of about 111% year-on-year and about 88% sequentially. This translates into an EBITDA margin of 15.48% for the quarter compared to 11.46% in Q1 FY26 and 11.29% in Q4 FY26.

evidence.fact: Profit after tax for Q1 FY27 stood at approximately INR 7.39 crore with a PAT margin of 8.9%.
evidence.quote: Profit after tax for the quarter stood at approximately INR7.39 crore compared to INR4.04 crore in Q1 FY26 and INR3.35 crore in Q4 FY26, a growth of approximately 82.6% year-on-year and 120.6% subsequently. Over PAT margin for the quarter came in at 8.9% compared to 7.63% a year ago.

evidence.fact: Nupur Recyclers imports approximately 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes of scrap metal annually across stainless steel, zinc, and aluminium.
evidence.quote: Every year, we import approximately 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes of scrap metal, spread across three metals: around 4,000 tonnes of stainless steel, 3,000 tonnes of zinc, and 2,000 tonnes of aluminium.

evidence.fact: Nupur Extrusion in Sampla has an installed capacity of 2,400 tons per annum and uses 1,800 tons per annum.
evidence.quote: So, we have another facility Nupur Extrusion in Sampla, Haryana. This aluminum extrusion we are producing here. 2,400 tons per annum is its installed capacity and still we are using 1,800 tons per annum. It's running at 75% right now.

evidence.fact: Frank Metals' Palwal facility produces 2,500 metric tons of zinc ingots per annum and 1,200 metric tons of aluminium ingots per annum at 100% capacity utilization.
evidence.quote: So, if I talk about the Frank Metals Recycling, it is a facility in Palwal, Haryana. So, we are producing zinc ingot 2,500 metric ton per annum. Capacity is the same, 2,500 metric ton per annum is utilized by 100%. Frank Metals Aluminum ingots 1,200 metric ton per annum. Capacity is also same, it's utilized by 100%.

evidence.fact: Management stated that the company is almost debt-free at its core and intends to fund ongoing expansions largely through internal accruals.
evidence.quote: We are almost debt-free company at our core and we intend to fund our ongoing expansion plans including the Sampla facility, Frank Metals aluminum extrusion investment and the upcoming LFP plant largely through internal accruals other than relying on external borrowings.

evidence.fact: The Board of Directors decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year 2025-26 to conserve profits.
evidence.quote: With a view to conserve the profits, the Board of Directors decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year 2025-26.

evidence.fact: An amount of ₹ 1,744.93 lakhs was transferred to the Capital Reserve during the year.
evidence.quote: During the year, an amount of ₹1,744.93 lakhs was transferred to the Capital Reserve.

evidence.fact: Management assured that current geopolitical environments have not had a material impact on operations because scrap is sourced from multiple geographies.
evidence.quote: I would like to assure you that this has not had a material impact on our operations. The reason is simple: we do not depend on any single country or region for our raw material. We source our scrap metal from multiple geographies the United States, Europe, the Middle East and Australia which gives us the flexibility to reroute our sourcing if any one region faces disruption.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 to 3 months): Management stated that the Sampla LFP battery recycling facility is expected to become operational over the next 2 to 3 months.
evidence.quote: It is against this backdrop that we are setting up a new facility in Sampla, Haryana with 6,000 tons LFP battery recycling, lithium iron phosphate battery recycling plant. Spread across 5 acres, expected to become operational over next 2 to 3 months.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (this financial year end): Management expects the Nupur Extrusion plant capacity to increase to about 350 tons per month by the end of this financial year.
evidence.quote: We already ordered one more Chinese automatic machine which is 4 inches machine. So, it should be in for the next two or three quarters or maybe this financial year end. We will go by about 350 tons per month.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next two to three months): Management stated that the Sampla plant for zinc and aluminium ingots will be ready for manufacturing in the next two to three months.
evidence.quote: So, sir, regarding Sampla plant, already the land is purchased in which construction is in progress. And in the next two to three months it will be ready for manufacturing.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY26): The company did not recommend any dividend for the financial year 2025-26.
evidence.quote: During the Financial Year, the Board of Directors has not recommended any dividend.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: Equity shares against convertible warrants are to be allotted within 18 months from the date of warrant allotment upon receipt of the balance 75% issue price.
evidence.quote: Fully paid up Equity Shares of face value Rs. 10/- each of the Company against each such warrant shall be allotted on receipt of balance 75% of the issue price for each such warrant and the same shall be allotted within 18 months from the date of allotment of such warrants.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: The shareholders approved the re-appointment of Kapal Kumar Vohra as Independent Director for a second term of five years from August 29, 2025, to August 28, 2030.
evidence.quote: approves the re-appointment of Mr. Kapal Kumar Vohra (DIN: 07384162) as an Independent Director (Non-Executive) for a second consecutive term of five years from August 29, 2025, to August 28, 2030.
